content: The Student National Medical Association (SNMA) is recognized as the oldest and largest student-led organization in the United States that is specifically dedicated to addressing the needs and concerns of medical students of color. Its membership includes over 6,000 individuals, comprising medical students, pre-medical students, residents, and physicians. The SNMA was established in 1964 by medical students from Howard University and Meharry Medical College. For over 40 years, the organization has been committed to serving both underserved communities and medical students. SNMA chapters, which are based at medical schools and some colleges across the United States, implement various programs and activities at the local level. The programs developed by the SNMA are specifically designed to address the healthcare needs of underserved populations and communities of color. Furthermore, the organization is dedicated to ensuring that medical education and healthcare services are culturally sensitive and tailored to the needs of diverse populations. It also strives to increase the number of African-American, Latino, and other underrepresented students of color who enter and successfully complete medical school. The SNMA is committed to supporting both current and future underrepresented minority medical students. It aims to address the needs of underserved communities while increasing the number of physicians who are not only clinically excellent but also culturally competent and socially conscious. There are over 130 SNMA chapters located at medical schools nationwide, and more than 70 undergraduate institutions host Minority Association of Pre-medical Students (MAPS) chapters. Official SNMA and MAPS chapters are recognized by the national SNMA through the annual submission of chapter renewal forms. Active and Associate members of the SNMA are national dues-paying members and are not required to be affiliated with a specific chapter. Similar to regional governance, chapters operate independently but must adhere to the national Constitution and Bylaws of the SNMA.
